page: The Vultr vc2-2c-4gb is a virtual machine offering within the Cloud Compute product line, delivering entry-level x86_64 compute capacity. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, configured with one physical core and two threads to present two shared vCPUs. The CPU subsystem includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for vector and cryptographic extensions including AVX, AVX-512, AES, and BMI2. The instance includes 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per vCPU, 80 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and one complimentary public IPv4 address. It does not include dedicated GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results characterize the instance within the lower performance tiers, consistent with shared-core virtualized hosting. The server achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 738.0 and a multi-core score of 1322.0, alongside a PassMark CPU rating of 2470.92. In stress-ng testing, it registered 1226.09 in single-core and 2501.8 in multi-core metrics. Memory throughput tests show 176.23 GB/sec for small cached reads, falling to 19.26 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 16.87 GB/sec for large writes. In operational benchmarks, the platform completed 1.36 million Redis SET operations per second and delivered 1.8 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The shared CPU allocation model and modest per-core throughput introduce latency variance during periods of host resource contention, making it unsuited for CPU-bound computations or real-time low-latency services. However, the bundling of 80 GB of high-speed local NVMe storage with 4.0 GB of memory offers qualitative cost efficiency for resource-light setups. This instance profile aligns with lightweight web servers, staging and test environments, small internal databases, microservices, and automated background jobs with modest throughput demands.
